liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Lost Sailor** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls the Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance the best pairing they have heard; Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance sets the tone, with strong Weir vocals and Garcia leading well [8][10][13]
- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): The band produces a good jam in Bird Song [18][19]
- **Big River** (2 reviews): Garcia and Brent both take hot solos on Big River [18][19]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Garcia tears it up on Minglewood [18][19]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Attendee recommends China Cat Sunflower as the sampler track, saying it might blow you away [9]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' opens with a circus-style theme the reviewer had not heard the band play before [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **It's not Brent's Birthday**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-07-11.152769.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd81-07-11.senn441.munder.7370.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 169 min; rated 3.92/5 by 26 [3]. Said about its sound: Attendee says Garcia was on form and the sound was excellent, which the audience recording captures [9]
- **gd1981-07-11.176353.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 171 min [4]
- **gd81-07-11.set2-sbd.fink.14020.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 106 min; rated 4.08/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: Soundboard covers only part of set two; the later portion is audience-sourced. The soundboard part sounds excellent; Dynamic range is somewhat squashed, but the highs are pleasing and cymbals sound natural with real depth [10][13]
- **gd1981-07-11.175192.sbd.tape2.miller.remaster.flac1644**: soundboard; 13 songs; 106 min [6]. Said about its sound: This remaster repairs the vocal phase problem, fixes levels and repatches the soundboard source [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Dead show; they lived about 25 miles away across the Illinois border and had friends working Alpine security [17]
- Reviewer ranks this among the most complex shows of 1981, with a jazzy vibe like Long Beach [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-07-11.152769.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > unknown deck; Jim Vita's 1st generation cassettes [1]. Also: First-generation recording came from Jim Vita; Charlie Miller did the transfer and coordinated the release; A Sennheiser 421 source from Rick Martin and Willy patches brief gaps in the Bird Song transition and post-Truckin' jam [1]
- **gd81-07-11.senn441.munder.7370.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421 [3]. Also: Commenter notes the listing says Sennheiser 421 but the uploaded file name references a 441; Chain is Sennheiser 421 to CM, then DAT, then CD, via Rick Martin; Willy seeded it to etree [3][12]
- **gd1981-07-11.176353.aud.bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer & Mastering by Ray Ackerman Edited & Processed w/ add'l Mastering by Joe Noel January 28, 2026; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > Sony TC-D5 > Master Cassettes (Maxell XLIIS-90's) [4]. Also: Jon Bernstein recorded this audience tape; Ray Ackerman did the transfer. Taper apparently sat up front under the shed [4]
- **gd81-07-11.set2-sbd.fink.14020.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1981-07-11.175192.sbd.tape2.miller.remaster.flac1644**: transferred by Remastered by Charlie Miller  November 20, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette > DAT > CD [6]. Also: Remaster of an earlier soundboard release; only tape 2 is in the vault, with source files from Alan J. Fink [6]
